subject: physics

moments.title: Dirac predicts monopoles
moments.body: Dirac shows that if even one magnetic monopole exists anywhere in the universe, all electric charge must be quantised. He calls the conclusion 'one of the strangest in physics'.
moments.takeaway: Charge quantisation might be a consequence of monopoles.

moments.title: GUT monopoles
moments.body: Grand Unified Theories predict heavy magnetic monopoles (~10^16 GeV). If inflation occurred, almost all would have been diluted away.

moments.title: Cabrera's Valentine's Day event
moments.body: On 14 February 1982, Cabrera's superconducting loop registers a single event consistent with a monopole passing through. The event is never reproduced. Was it real?
moments.takeaway: One of the most tantalising single events in physics history.

moments.title: Still nothing
moments.body: Searches with MoEDAL (LHC), IceCube and direct-detection experiments have found no monopoles. Limits exclude vast regions of parameter space.
moments.takeaway: If monopoles exist, they are extraordinarily rare.

now.title: Where we are today
now.body: Monopoles are predicted by most GUTs. None has been observed. Analogue monopoles (Dirac strings) have been simulated in spin ice and BECs.
now.open_questions: Do monopoles exist? Were they all inflated away?

reflection: Cabrera saw one event. Sagan said: 'Extraordinary claims require extraordinary evidence.' When is one event ever enough?
